questions.stem: Why are unsaturated fats (oils) liquid at room temperature while saturated fats are solid?

options.text: The C=C double bonds create kinks in the chains, preventing close packing and weakening intermolecular forces
Unsaturated fats have lower molecular masses

questions.explanation: The C=C double bonds in unsaturated fats create kinks in the hydrocarbon chains. These kinks prevent the molecules from packing closely together, resulting in weaker van der Waals forces and lower melting points. Saturated chains pack closely, giving stronger forces and higher melting points.

questions.stem: How does a soap molecule remove grease from a surface?

options.text: The soap reacts chemically with the grease to dissolve it
The hydrophobic tail dissolves in grease while the hydrophilic head stays in water, forming micelles that carry grease away
The soap neutralises the grease with its alkaline properties
The soap evaporates the grease by raising its temperature

questions.explanation: Soap molecules have a dual structure: a hydrophobic (water-hating) tail that dissolves into grease and a hydrophilic (water-loving) head that stays in water. The molecules surround grease droplets forming spherical clusters called micelles, which are then carried away in the water.
